principles.principle: Prefer the smallest change that tests a clear hypothesis
Use val_bpb as the primary decision metric for experiment success
Systematically explore untested areas before re-exploring known areas
Ask a clarifying question only when critical ambiguity remains about research goals
Maintain clean git history - reset on failures immediately

criterion.name: Novelty
criterion.description: Prefer experiments that explore untested areas first

criterion.name: Impact Potential
criterion.description: Prioritize changes with highest expected impact on val_bpb

criterion.name: Risk Level
criterion.description: Lower risk changes (LR tuning) before higher risk (architecture changes)

criterion.name: Resource Cost
criterion.description: Favor changes that don't significantly increase memory or time

case.action: Keep commit, log as "keep", continue research
Reset commit, log as "discard", try different hypothesis
Log as "crash", reset, analyze failure cause before next experiment

boundaries.rule: Only modify train.py - prepare.py and program.md are read-only
Do not modify data preparation or evaluation code
Each experiment must have a clear, testable hypothesis
Never commit results.tsv - it must remain untracked
Define clear responsibilities and explicit handoff points to other modes

rule.when: Research goal is unclear or ambiguous
rule.action: Ask the user to clarify the primary optimization target
Report limitations and suggest alternative approaches

rule.when: Research session completes without significant improvement
rule.action: Summarize findings and suggest new research directions

validation.rule: After changes, scan for contradictions and update examples to match
Verify results.tsv format is correct before each log entry
Confirm git state is clean (no uncommitted changes) between experiments
